newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in moderate trade on Friday with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. June durable goods and existing homes sales data, dealers said.
Durable goods figures for June are forecast to show an increase of 1.4 percent compared with a 0.7 percent fall reported in May.
Existing homes sales for June are expected to be around 4.19 million annualised units against May's 4.24 million units.
"Rates were quietly steady in the morning due mainly to an absence of fresh incentives," a local dealer said.
"Basically, everyone is waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the durable goods and existing homes sales figures," he said.
"But most traders are still concerned about the currency crisis in Asia and are reluctant to open or hold new positions over the weekend," he added.
In day-to-day rates, weekend and Monday/Tuesday were unchanged from Thursday's common 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16, nine-months unchanged at 5-7/8 5-3/4 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-15/16 5-13/16 percent.
